summary: WebSocket-driven remote shell and server-commanded self-upgrade on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs an agent process that opens an outbound WebSocket connection to a configured server and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that (a) spawn an interactive PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, pwsh on Windows) and forward server-supplied bytes into it, (b) read and write files on the host, (c) perform git push operations, and (d) execute arbitrary conversation-driven actions. A dedicated `upgrade_agent` message type causes the agent to write and run an upgrade script that invokes `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the public registry in a detached process, then restarts the systemd/launchd service. Together these give whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint full remote code execution on the installer's machine, persistent control across restarts, and the ability to force a pull of any future published version of the package. service/linux.js also modifies the user's shell PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin`. The `ping` matches in the bundled msal-browser.min.js and in yeaft/tools/web-search.js correspond to unrelated identifiers (Microsoft MSAL browser library, web-search tooling) rather than exfiltration commands.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
